clips.description: A cannula is inserted into the anterior chamber of an eye with a traumatic cataract and fibrotic capsule. A white, cloudy substance (triamcinolone) is injected, which stains and highlights prolapsed vitreous strands in the anterior chamber. Following this, a second cannula irrigates the anterior chamber with a clear solution (BSS) to wash away excess triamcinolone.
clips.transcript: We'll start off with injection of some triamcinolone to localize and visualize the vitreous. We'll inject it in a dilute formulation and then irrigate some BSS in the anterior chamber to isolate where these triamcinolone crystals will localize and stain the vitreous.

clips.description: A viscoelastic cannula is used to inject a clear, gel-like ophthalmic viscosurgical device (OVD) into the anterior chamber, deepening it and pushing back the iris. The tip of the cannula is then used to mechanically dissect and release adhesions (posterior synechiae) between the iris and the anterior lens capsule, revealing a large area of zonular dialysis inferonasally.
clips.transcript: Viscoelastic is injected and we'll release some of that posterior synechiae present on the pupil margin and there you can see some vitreous present at the infranasal pupil margin as well as the edge of the lens... It's almost about 120 degrees or greater zonular dialysis.

anomalies: Vitreous Prolapse / Anterior Vitrectomy
clips.description: The capsulorhexis is initiated with micro-scissors due to the highly fibrotic nature of the anterior capsule, which could not be punctured with a standard cystotome. Capsulorhexis forceps are then used to grasp the created flap, but propagation is difficult. The surgeon alternates between shearing and stretching techniques with two instruments (forceps and a second instrument for counter-traction) to manage the tear. The rhexis tears out superiorly. Ultimately, micro-scissors are used again to cut the remaining fibrotic tissue, resulting in an irregular, discontinuous anterior capsular opening.
clips.transcript: We've decided to do the capsulorhexis first prior to the vitrectomy... we're going to use some sharp micro scissors to actually start the capsulorhexis... We do get an initial tear and we'll use a couple micro forceps... we basically move to a stretch technique... and then turn the flap over to a shearing technique... we will then proceed to use a pair of micro scissors to complete the rhexis here... and we have now a capsulorhexis albeit a discontinuous one and an irregular one.

anomalies: Vitreous Prolapse / Anterior Vitrectomy
Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: A bimanual approach is used for anterior vitrectomy. An irrigation cannula maintains anterior chamber stability while a vitrectomy cutter is used to remove the previously stained vitreous strands from the anterior chamber, particularly around the pupil margin in the area of zonular dialysis. Viscoelastic is injected to reform the chamber before the instruments are withdrawn.
clips.transcript: At this point now, we'll proceed to do some limited vitrectomy here using a bimanual technique through the limbal incisions... basically trim the vitreous from the pupil margin... keep the chamber formed before pulling out with our irrigation by injecting viscoelastic.

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: A phaco probe and a chopper instrument are introduced into the anterior chamber. The surgeon embeds the phaco probe into the nucleus and uses a vertical chop technique to crack the nucleus in half. Each heminucleus is then elevated toward the iris plane and emulsified. Care is taken to work away from the area of zonular dialysis. Viscoelastic is added to maintain chamber depth and protect the capsular bag throughout the process.
clips.transcript: We will proceed to phacoemulsification. The lens itself is moderately dense. We proceed to a vertical chop and crack the lens in half and we're going to actually do a little bit of a hemi flip here bringing each hemi section one at a time to the iris plane to phaco and emulsify the lens.

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: A 27-gauge cannula attached to a syringe is used for manual irrigation and aspiration of the remaining lens cortex. The surgeon carefully strips cortical material from the capsular bag fornix, being gentle due to the zonular weakness. The capsular bag is visibly mobile during this step.
clips.transcript: And now we'll basically remove the cortex. Now this is certainly a hazardous point in time and we've decided to use a manual technique, using a 27 gauge cannula to aspirate the cortex.

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: The capsular bag is inflated with cohesive viscoelastic. A capsular tension ring (CTR) is then injected into the capsular bag. A Sinskey hook is used to dial the ring completely into the equatorial fornix of the bag, which expands and stabilizes the capsular bag in the presence of zonular dialysis.
clips.transcript: At this point in time we'll reinflate the capsule bag with some cohesive viscoelastic... we place a CTR by injecting it toward the dialysis. You can see the bag is now expanded, the capsule seems to be well-supported...

anomalies: Vitreous Prolapse / Anterior Vitrectomy
clips.description: With the anterior chamber filled with viscoelastic, a vitrectomy cutter is used in a 'dry' technique to remove residual vitreous strands from the inferonasal quadrant. A Kuglen hook is used simultaneously to retract the iris, providing better access and protecting the iris from the cutter.
clips.transcript: And then we'll finish off with just trimming whatever vitreous may be present in that inferior and inferonasal quadrant, using a dry technique under viscoelastic, using a Kuglen hook to push away the iris there.

clips.description: A Cionni-type capsular tension segment (CTS), a hemi-ring device, is inserted into the capsular bag using forceps. Both eyelets of the CTS are tucked under the anterior capsular rim in the area of greatest zonular weakness.
clips.transcript: And now the capsular tension segment is used. This is a coat hanger-like device, a hemi-ring. Both islets are placed under the anterior capsule.

clips.transcript: The central islet will be used in conjunction with an iris hook, which we place upside down through the islet. And this provides really broad support in the area where the zonules are weak.

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: The supporting iris hook is removed, and the CTS is maneuvered from the capsular bag into the anterior chamber. A scleral incision is made externally. A 25-gauge needle is passed through the scleral incision into the anterior chamber. A 7-0 Gore-Tex suture is threaded through the needle tip (docking technique) and then passed through the eyelet of the CTS. Both ends of the suture now exit through the scleral incision.
clips.transcript: Now the CTS is now mobilized... and we will plan for suture placement... using a 7-0 Gore-Tex suture here in an ab-externo docking technique to place it through the CTS.

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: Using two pairs of forceps, the surgeon ties the external Gore-Tex suture ends into a slip knot. This allows for adjustable tension to be applied to the CTS and capsular bag later in the procedure.

clips.description: A pre-operative slit-lamp view of the patient's right eye, showing a cataractous lens. The lens is observed to shake and oscillate with eye movement, a sign of phacodonesis or zonular laxity.
clips.transcript: Upon initial inspection of the lens through the microscope, we noticed that the lens shakes and oscillates in an unusual manner indicating phacodenesis and likely loose zonules.

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: A cystotome is used to puncture and lift the edge of the laser-created anterior capsule flap. Due to zonular laxity, the capsule is very mobile. Additional viscoelastic (Healon) is injected. Capsulorhexis forceps are then used to grasp and remove the free-floating circular capsule flap.
clips.transcript: When we attempt to pierce the anterior capsule, there's increased laxity noted with the anterior capsule. We then use Healon to fill the anterior chamber. ... As we perform our capsulorhexis, we note there is definitely less resistance to pulling on the anterior capsule...

clips.description: An irrigation/aspiration (I/A) tip is used to remove the residual soft lens cortex from the capsular bag. The edge of the capsulorhexis is observed to move centrally as cortex is aspirated, indicating significant zonular weakness.
clips.transcript: Next we begin removal of cortex with the I/A tip. But as I see the anterior capsule edge at 9 o'clock move centrally as the cortex is aspirated...

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: Due to the observed capsular bag instability, the I/A tip is removed. Four capsular retractors (hooks) are inserted through paracentesis incisions and hooked onto the capsulorhexis rim to stabilize and support the capsular bag.
clips.transcript: ...the decision is made to place more viscoelastic into the eye, remove the I/A tip, and then place capsular retractors to support the capsular bag...

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: With the capsular bag now stabilized by the retractors, the I/A tip is reintroduced to safely remove the remaining cortical material without causing further stress on the zonules.
clips.transcript: With the capsule retractors now in place, we can more confidently and safely remove the remaining cortex with less concern about creating zonular dehiscence during this process.

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: A capsular tension ring (CTR) is injected into the equatorial region of the capsular bag using an injector. The ring expands within the bag to provide long-term circumferential support.
clips.transcript: Once the cortex has been removed and the posterior capsule polished, a capsular tension ring is inserted to provide more stability for the capsular bag.

clips.description: Due to the density of the nucleus, the phaco probe is removed. The surgeon uses two micro-instruments (choppers/manipulators) to bimanually crack the nucleus along the sculpted grooves. During this maneuver, significant zonular weakness becomes evident as the capsular bag equator is visible from the 9 to 12 o'clock position.
clips.transcript: After we've created our two grooves, we find that there's a posterior plate that is difficult to crack. So we fill the eye with a generous amount of cohesive viscoelastic and we use two micro instruments to manually rotate and crack this lens. But in the process of cracking the lens we see from 9 o'clock until 12 o'clock in the video that the equator of the bag is visible, indicating loss of zonular integrity in that area.

clips.description: Using capsulorhexis forceps, the surgeon creates a circular opening in the anterior capsule of the traumatically dislocated lens. The tear is guided carefully around the periphery to create a continuous capsular flap, following the contour of the subluxated lens equator.
clips.transcript: The capsulorhexis here is performed to follow the contour of the lens equator, making sure we leave enough of an anterior capsular shelf to place capsular retractors...

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: Three capsular retractors are inserted through paracentesis ports. The hooks engage the edge of the capsulorhexis to stabilize and center the capsular bag, compensating for the area of zonular dialysis.
clips.transcript: These are the MST capsular retractors, very helpful in these significant zonulopathy cases, typically placing two or three along the area of the zonular dialysis.

anomalies: Vitreous Prolapse / Anterior Vitrectomy
clips.description: A phaco handpiece and a chopper instrument are introduced into the anterior chamber. The surgeon uses a vertical chop technique to break the nucleus into smaller fragments, which are then emulsified and aspirated from the capsular bag.
clips.transcript: ...a phaco chop, and this phaco goes fairly uneventfully, making sure we keep that chamber formed to avoid any vitreous prolapse...

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: A capsular tension ring (CTR) is injected into the capsular bag. A Sinskey hook is used to guide the CTR fully into the equatorial fornix of the bag, which helps to expand and stabilize it.
clips.transcript: We've now cleared the capsular bag, we'll keep the AC formed with viscoelastic, the capsular tension ring is used, CTR here, and this will round out the capsular bag...

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: A partial-thickness scleral groove is created with a blade near the limbus, in the area corresponding to the zonular dialysis.
clips.transcript: One and a half millimeters back from the posterior edge of that blue zone is where we make our groove.

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: A capsular tension segment (CTS) is placed into the capsular bag. A 7-0 GORE-TEX suture is passed from outside the eye (ab externo) through the scleral groove using a 25-gauge needle for docking. The suture is threaded through the CTS eyelet and externalized, preparing it for fixation to the scleral wall.
clips.transcript: This is the capsular tension segment being placed here, and we're going to use 7-0 GORE-TEX... using a docking approach, ab externo with the 25 gauge needle... this will support that bag long term with GORE-TEX suture.

anomalies: Zonular Dialysis / Dehiscence / CTR / CTS Insertion
clips.description: Using two pairs of microforceps, the surgeon ties the externalized GORE-TEX suture to fixate the CTS to the scleral wall. The suture knot is then trimmed and carefully buried into the previously created scleral groove. The final view shows a well-centered IOL and artificial iris complex.
clips.transcript: Finally, we will lock that suture in place and bury the knot...
